metallio.sxolio1: Hydrean shipowner, notable and politician, whose family had in its possession a large part of the island’s merchant fleet.
metallio.sxolio2: In 1823 he enters the central political scene as plenipotentiary of Hydra in the 2nd National Assembly of Astros (1823).
metallio.sxolio3: He shared a close bond with his older brother, Lazaros, whom he considered «as a second parent». Throughout the Struggle, he was somehow carrying out his brother’s decisions.

metallio.sxolio1: Naval officer and one of the greatest British Philhellenes, who in 1824 wrote and submitted to the Greek Government a memorandum on necessary reforms in the Greek navy.
metallio.sxolio2: Governor of the pioneering steam-powered corvette «Perseverance» («Karteria»), which was built in London and sailed into the Argolic Gulf in early September 1826.
metallio.sxolio3: In May 1828, during an attempt to occupy Aetoliko, he sustained a serious injury to his hand. Before being transferred to Zakynthos, to receive medical care, he contracted tetanus and died.

metallio.sxolio1: He served as admiral of the fleet of Psara, which included 41 ships, of which four belonged to himself (Leonidas, Sokratis, Miltiadis).
metallio.sxolio2: Anastasios Orlandos called him «Nestor of Psara».
metallio.sxolio3: When in 1827 the British Thomas Alexander Cochrane was appointed by the National Assembly of Troezen as Admiral of the Greek Fleet, he was summoned from Aegina where he was at the time, to assist in the operations of Attica. During his journey to Piraeus, he fell ill with pneumonia and was forced to return to Aegina, where he finally died on the 19th of April.

metallio.sxolio1: Born into a prominent Phanariote family, he arrived in June of 1821 in the Peloponnese as plenipotentiary of the General Commissioner of the Authority.
metallio.sxolio2: He was the head of the Greek forces in the victorious battle at the site of Petra in Boeotia (12 September 1829), the last battle of the Revolution.
metallio.sxolio3: He was elected President of the Legislative in the 1st National Assembly of Epidaurus.

metallio.sxolio1: There are more than one versions about his birthplace, the prevailing ones being Mavromati of Karditsa and Skoulikaria of Arta.
metallio.sxolio2: In connection to the siege of Athens, on 22 April 1827, during a minor clash at Phaleron, he was mortally wounded.
metallio.sxolio3: At the outbreak of the Revolution in West Greece (May 1821) he joins the revolutionary forces. Until the middle of 1822 he had emerged as a predominant figure of the Agrafiote brigand group (armatoliki) and chiliarch (commanding officer of a thousand soldiers) of the revolutionary administration.

metallio.sxolio1: Son of the ship-owner and merchant, Dimitris Vokos, he was born on the island of Hydra (or, according to another version, in Fylla of Euboea) and at the age of 11 he entered the maritime profession, continuing the family tradition.
metallio.sxolio2: From January 1822, after the retirement of Iakovakis Tompazis, he was appointed admiral of Hydra and head commander of the three-island fleet, taking part in a series of naval battles throughout the course of the Struggle.
metallio.sxolio3: He played a leading role in the victory of the Greek naval forces over the Turkish-Egyptian fleet in the naval battle of Gerontas (29 August 1824).

metallio.sxolio1: Born in Dimitsana, he attended clerical studies and soon became protosyncellus (principal deputy of the bishop) and then bishop. In 1818 he was initiated in the Society of Friends.
metallio.sxolio2: On 24 March 1821 he blessed the arms of the revolutionaries in Agios Georgios square in Patras and the following day he participated in the formation of the Achaean Directory.
metallio.sxolio3: From 1822 to 1824 he participated outside Greece, together with Georgios Mavromichalis, in an official diplomatic mission to Italy, with the aim to arrange a meeting with the pope of Rome.

metallio.sxolio1: His fame as military genius spread across Europe after the fall of Tripolitsa and the final defeat of Dramali in the summer of 1822.
metallio.sxolio2: Persecuted during the Bavarian Regency, he was tried and condemned to death. Finally, he was granted amnesty by young Otto.
metallio.sxolio3: Known also as the «old man of the Morea», he was identified with the armed struggle, radiating charm, as a leading figure of the Revolution, both to Greeks and Philhellenes.

metallio.sxolio1: Born in a Maniot family of notables, he served as President of the 2nd National Assembly, which convened at Astros of Kynouria in March 1823.
metallio.sxolio2: After the occupation of Kalamata by the forces of the revolution, he formed the Messinian Senate and signed the revolutionary proclamation titled «Warning to the European courts».
metallio.sxolio3: His family constituted one of the strongest nuclei of opposition to Ioannis Kapodistrias. Two of its members assassinated the Governor, outside the church of Saint Spyridon in Nafplion.

metallio.sxolio1: His political vision encompassed the creation of a multi-national Balkan democracy, with the Greek element predominant in it.
metallio.sxolio2: Although he had received a passport from the Austrian police, with the aim to travel down to Greece and put in action his revolutionary plan, he was arrested at Trieste, following the treason of a Greek merchant. He was interrogated, imprisoned, tortured for six months and finally, shackled, was transferred to Belgrade, where he was put to death together with his seven comrades in the Nebojša Tower, in June 1798.
metallio.sxolio3: His revolutionary war song «Thourios» enjoyed enormous dissemination in the area of the Balkans, emboldening the subjugated populations and instigating an uprising against the Ottoman dynast.

metallio.sxolio1: High-ranking officer of the Russian army, who undertook the leadership of the Society of Friends after Ioannis Kapodistrias declined it.
metallio.sxolio2: He distinguished himself in the wars against Napoleon. In the battle of Dresden, on 27th August 1813, he lost his right hand.
metallio.sxolio3: He crossed the Prouthos river on 22 February 1821 and two days later he raised the flag of the Revolution at Jassy of Moldavia-Wallachia.

metallio.sxolio1: Born in Kerpini in 1791 and member of the Society of Friends since 1819, in January 1821 he participated in the secret assembly of Vostitsa.
metallio.sxolio2: He took part in the National Assemblies as plenipotentiary of the province of Kalavryta, which, on the eve of the Revolution of 1821, he governed together with his father Asimakis.
metallio.sxolio3: After Otto’s arrival he was appointed as Counsellor of State (1833) and plenipotentiary royal court commissioner (1834), while from October 1835 he served as vice-president of the Council of State (1835), a position he held until his death.

metallio.sxolio1: He was the fearless captain of the famous brig «Aris» and squadron leader under Andreas Miaoulis.
metallio.sxolio2: Heroic Hydrean admiral, who fell in the naval battle of Sfakteria in 1825, defying death during the attack launched by Ibrahim’s forces.
metallio.sxolio3: In 1825 he sailed into Neokastro with food and ammunition, managing to provide with supplies the fort that was under siege by Ibrahim.

metallio.sxolio1: Together with Georgios Panou, on 3rd April 1821 he raised the flag of the Revolution at the Chancellery (Headquarters) of Spetses.
metallio.sxolio2: He was appointed by D. Ypsilantis as ephor of Spetses and in autumn 1823 he came, leading a small fleet, to Missolonghi, where he remained until 1824.
metallio.sxolio3: He served as Vice-President of the Executive that was formed in October 1824, with Georgios Kountouriotis as President.
